t: Under IMT 35 (hired vehicles driven by hirer), before each hiring the hirer must
o: enter into a hire contract and complete and sign a supplementary proposal form
deposit the IDV of the vehicle with the insurer
obtain a cover note in his own name
be named in the policy schedule as a driver
e: IMT 35 makes the policy operative while the vehicle is let on hire only to a hirer who has entered into a hire contract, signed a supplementary proposal form and satisfied the insured that only a duly licensed driver with a clean insurance record will drive.

t: What is the difference between IMT 36 and IMT 44 (indemnity to hirer under a package policy)?
o: IMT 36 is free while IMT 44 costs 1.5% of IDV
IMT 36 covers OD only and IMT 44 covers TP only
IMT 36 indemnifies the hirer only for loss arising from negligence of the insured or his employees, while IMT 44 extends to negligence of the owner or the hirer
IMT 36 applies to two wheelers and IMT 44 to cars
e: IMT 36 indemnifies the hirer against loss, damage and liability arising by reason of the negligence of the insured or his employees; IMT 44 (package) and IMT 45 (liability only) indemnify the hirer for liability arising while let on hire including the hirer's own negligence, on additional premium.

t: IMT 37A covers legal liability to non-fare paying passengers in a commercial vehicle who are
o: fare paying passengers up to the licensed capacity
not employees of the insured, being the charterer or representative of the charterer, or persons directly connected with the journey
employees of the insured not covered under the WC Act
e: IMT 37 covers employees who are not workmen under the WC Act plus charterers; IMT 37A covers only persons who are not employees - the charterer or his representative or any person directly connected with the journey - not carried for hire or reward.

t: IMT 38 (legal liability to fare paying passengers) cannot be granted in respect of
o: motor trade policies rateable under Classes E, F and G
e: Although IMT 38 is captioned for commercial and motor trade vehicles, the extension is not permitted for motor trade policies rateable under sub-sections E, F and G of the Commercial Vehicles Tariff.

t: A goods carrier owner wants WC Act liability cover for 9 loaders carried in the truck in addition to the driver. The correct endorsement is
o: IMT 39A, provided special permission from the registration authority for carrying more than six employees is obtained
IMT 39, which covers any number of employees
e: IMT 39 covers persons employed in loading/unloading up to the number permitted (not exceeding seven including driver and cleaner); carriage of more than six employees (excluding driver) is covered by IMT 39A only where the insured has special permission from the registering authority.

t: Under IMT 41 (Motor Trade Class F) the geographical area for Section II(i) (liability under the MV Act) is
o: the district of the dealer's premises
the same 80 km radius as the OD section
India, while all other sections are limited to a radius of 80 or 120 km from the insured's address
e: IMT 41 defines the geographical area for new vehicles bearing trade certificates: under Section II(i) - India; under all other sections - within a radius of 80 or 120 km (as opted and paid for) from the insured's address.

t: A truck with a private carrier permit insured with IMT 42 is damaged while carrying a neighbour's goods for a consideration. The insurer
o: is not liable for the OD loss or any third party liability, as the vehicle was carrying goods not belonging to the insured
pays 50% of the OD loss on non-standard basis
pays both claims after charging the public carrier premium difference
pays the OD claim but denies TP liability
e: IMT 42 (private carriers) provides that the insurer shall not be liable for loss or damage to the vehicle and/or any third party liability if at the time of accident the vehicle is carrying goods not belonging to the insured (for liability only policies the OD words are deleted).

t: Under IMT 43 (theft and conversion risk for hired vehicles) which statement is correct?
o: Theft of accessories by the hirer is covered
The premium is Rs 100 flat per vehicle
NCB applies to the additional premium as it is part of OD
The additional premium of 1.5% of IDV is not eligible for NCB, and indemnity applies only to theft/conversion of the entire vehicle
e: IMT 43 deletes the theft/conversion exclusion in IMT 35 at 1.5% of IDV; indemnity is limited to theft or conversion of the entire vehicle and NCB is not applicable to this additional premium.

t: Legal liability to passengers carried in an ambulance or hearse rated under Class D is covered by
e: IMT 46 (legal liability to passengers excluding employees) applies to ambulances/hearses under Class D and to motor trade vehicles; passenger liability premium is Rs 60 for ambulances and Rs 115 for hearses.

t: The own damage premium of a car before NCB is Rs 18,000 and the insured has three consecutive claim-free years. The NCB amount is
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). GR 27: NCB for three consecutive claim-free years is 35%; 35% of Rs 18,000 = Rs 6,300, leaving a net OD premium of Rs 11,700.

t: Under GR 40 N.B.3 the additional premium for reinstating the IMT 21 exclusions through IMT 23 is
o: 15% of the total gross OD premium before application of any discount
15% of the net OD premium after NCB
e: GR 40 N.B.3: exclusions under (a) of IMT 21 may be reinstated by payment of 15% of the total gross OD premium (before any discount) using IMT 23; the compulsory deductible cannot be removed.

t: Which discount is permissible on a fire and/or theft only cover under GR 45A for a private car?
o: Discount for voluntary deductible only; no other discount is permissible
e: GR 45A: compulsory deductibles, electrical fittings and CNG premiums and CPA premium apply; a discount may be granted for voluntary deductibles on private cars/two wheelers, but no other discount is permissible and a written request is required.

t: Under GR 45B (liability only with fire and/or theft) for a private car, which discounts are permissible?
o: NCB on the fire/theft components, voluntary deductible discount and Automobile Association discount
Only the NCB on the liability premium
e: GR 45B N.B. permits NCB on fire and/or theft components, discounts for voluntary deductibles for private cars/two wheelers, and the Automobile Association discount under GR 28.

t: For a driving school car with double clutches and brakes, under GR 44 the liability (TP) premium is
o: loaded by 60% like the OD premium
as per tariff without loading, while the OD premium is loaded by 60%
e: GR 44: vehicles used for driving tuition by an RTA-recognised school are charged the applicable OD premium plus 60% loading; the liability premium is as per tariff.

t: A goods carrier owner opts for additional towing charges of Rs 15,000 under GR 47. The additional premium rate is
e: GR 47 for other commercial vehicles: additional towing up to Rs 10,000 at 5%, and Rs 10,000 to Rs 20,000 at 7.5% of the additional amount opted.

t: An insured sells his private car carrying 50% NCB and buys a taxi. He asks for the NCB on the taxi policy. The office should
o: not allow any NCB, since NCB can be used only for a substituted vehicle of the same class
allow 50% on OD and nil on TP
e: GR 27: NCB follows the insured and can be used for a substituted vehicle of the same class only; a private car and a taxi are different classes, so no NCB is transferable.

t: A serving army officer's car policy expired while he was posted in a remote area, and he renews it 7 months later. His NCB
o: is allowed at half the earned slab
may be allowed, since for military personnel the grace period is up to 365 days depending on the individual case and proof
lapses, as the 90-day limit has passed
is allowed only if the car was laid up under IMT 11A
e: Normally NCB is allowed if the policy is renewed within 90 days of expiry; for military personnel the grace period can extend to 365 days depending on the case and proof.

t: A car is covered by two package policies from different insurers for exactly the same period. Under GR 24 (double insurance)
o: both policies continue and share claims
either policy may be cancelled as per the insured's choice, with pro-rata refund of the policy cancelled
the policy of the insurer with the higher premium is cancelled
the later-issued policy must be cancelled
e: Where one policy commences later, the later one is cancelled with pro-rata refund; if both have identical periods, either one is cancelled as per the insured's choice.

t: An insured cancels his private car policy (annual premium Rs 9,000, no claim) exactly 5 months after inception. The refund under GR 24 is
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). Cancellation by the insured attracts short period retention: exceeding 4 months but not exceeding 5 months = 60% retained (Rs 5,400); refund = Rs 9,000 - Rs 5,400 = Rs 3,600.

t: A dealer's Class F road risks policy cannot be used for vehicles
o: let out for hire or reward
received from customers for repair or service
e: Class F covers new unregistered vehicles and vehicles in the dealer's custody for repair/service, on named driver or trade certificate basis, but is not to be used for hire or reward.

t: Under a Class E road transit policy for brand new chassis with new tyres, the 50% limitation on tyres can be deleted on payment of
e: Deletion of the 50% limitation clause for tyres and tubes under Class E is permitted only for brand new vehicles with brand new tyres on payment of 1% of basic OD premium using IMT 62.

t: Which of the following is NOT a purpose for which a vehicle may be used under a trade certificate as per Rule 41 of CMVR?
o: Carrying goods for a customer for payment
Trial or demonstration for a prospective purchaser
Proceeding to or returning from a weighbridge or place of registration
Proceeding to a workshop for painting or fitting of a body
e: Rule 41 permits use for tests, registration/weighbridge trips, demonstration, delivery between dealers, workshop trips, transport terminals, exhibitions and removal by a financier - never for commercial carriage of goods.

t: Under the Class G tariff, two premises of a dealer situated within 450 metres of each other by road and insured under one policy
o: may be deemed to be one premises, or dealt with as separate premises if preferred
are rated as one premises compulsorily
must be insured under two separate policies
e: Premises within 450 metres by road of other premises belonging to the same owner under one policy may be deemed one premises or treated separately; each premises is rated separately on area and wages and multi-premises discounts of 20/25/30% may apply.

t: A mobile crane overturns while lifting a load at a site and is also damaged by a fire that breaks out on overturning. Under IMT 47 without the overturning extension, the insurer is liable for
o: nothing, as the vehicle was in use as a tool of trade
the fire damage only, since loss from overturning during operation as a tool of trade is excluded except loss arising directly from fire, explosion, self-ignition, lightning or theft
the entire loss including overturning damage
e: IMT 47(a) excludes Section I loss from overturning arising out of operation as a tool of trade except loss arising directly from fire, explosion, self-ignition, lightning or burglary/housebreaking/theft; para (a) is omitted where the overturning premium (0.5% of IDV) is paid.

t: A plough attached to an insured agricultural tractor under IMT 48 breaks when it strikes a buried rock while ploughing. The claim is
o: payable in full under Section I
not payable, as breakage of agricultural implements caused by ground obstruction is excluded
e: IMT 48 extends cover to trailers and agricultural implements (ploughs, harrows etc.) on additional premium but excludes breakage of any part of the agricultural trailer or implements caused by ground obstructions.

t: The minimum value for premium computation of a pedestrian-controlled agricultural tractor not exceeding 6 HP is
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). Class D vehicles have a minimum IDV of Rs 50,000, except pedestrian-controlled agricultural tractors not exceeding 6 HP for which it is Rs 10,000.

t: IMT 53 (specified attachments) provides that attachments listed in the schedule of attachments are covered
o: only while attached to the vehicle
without any IDV, at market value
as though each were the motor vehicle, whether attached or detached and out of use, up to the IDV set against it
e: IMT 53 covers scheduled attachments while attached to the vehicle or detached and out of use, as though each were the motor vehicle, with the IDV set against it; for pedestrian controlled tractors 'any standard attachment supplied by the makers' is inserted.

t: For which of the following Class D goods vehicles does the standard policy NOT permit use for hire or reward?
e: For Class D goods vehicles the standard policy allows use for hire or reward except agricultural and forestry vehicles, mobile shops and canteens, cinema film and publicity vans, pedestrian-controlled delivery trucks, goods carrying tractors, driving tuition vehicles and fire brigade/salvage corps vehicles.

t: A stolen vehicle is recovered by the police in a damaged condition before the claim is paid. The insured should be advised to
o: take delivery immediately and repair the vehicle
obtain a recovery memo from the police and have the vehicle surveyed at the police station before taking delivery
refuse to take delivery until the claim is settled
e: If the recovered vehicle is damaged, the insured is indemnified for damage while it was out of his custody; he should obtain a police recovery memo and get the vehicle surveyed at the police station before taking delivery.

t: The authenticity of the registration certificate and driving licence submitted for an OD claim can be checked on
e: RC and DL particulars are verified on the Parivahan website; the IIB portal is used to check the vehicle's previous claim history.

t: The balance payment in a theft claim (after an on-account payment) is released on receipt of
o: the final police investigation report, letter of indemnity and subrogation, and a discharge voucher in full and final settlement
e: After the on-account payment against a specially worded discharge, the balance is paid on receipt of the final police report after obtaining the indemnity and subrogation letter and a full and final discharge voucher.

t: In the standard OD claim flow chart, re-inspection of the repaired vehicle takes place
o: after the survey and before the survey report submission and bill check
e: Flow: intimation, validation, claim form, estimate, survey appointment, survey/re-inspection, survey report, bill check, vehicle record verification, claim note/approval, system processing, voucher and NEFT payment.

t: The minimum value for premium computation of a four wheeled passenger vehicle with carrying capacity of 12 passengers is
e: Four wheeled passenger vehicles carrying more than 6 but not more than 17 passengers have a minimum IDV of Rs 20,000; the corresponding three wheelers have Rs 25,000; 17-36 passengers Rs 30,000.

t: Under GR 36B the premium for optional PA cover to named persons in a private car (IMT 15) is, per Rs 10,000 of CSI,
e: GR 36B rates per Rs 10,000 CSI or part thereof: private car Rs 5, motorised two wheeler Rs 7, commercial vehicle Rs 6.

t: Compulsory third party motor insurance is NOT required for a vehicle with engine capacity below
e: The material notes that motor TP insurance is not required below 25 cc; separately, no licence is needed for vehicles not exceeding 50 cc provided the rider is at least 16 years old.

t: The registration certificate of a non-transport vehicle is valid for
o: 15 years from the date of issue, renewable for 5 years at a time
e: RC of non-transport vehicles is valid for 15 years and renewed for 5 years at a time; for transport vehicles RC validity depends on the fitness certificate.

t: A corporate agent may tie up with a maximum of how many insurers in each line of business?
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). Raised from 3 to 9 insurers per category (life, general, health) by the 2022 amendment to the Corporate Agents Regulations.

t: A private car (1800 cc) aged 5 years 2 months, IDV Rs 3,00,000, is damaged. Assessment before depreciation: metal parts Rs 50,000, airbags Rs 40,000, fibre glass parts Rs 10,000, labour Rs 15,000; salvage of damaged parts Rs 2,000. The amount payable is
e: Metal 40% (5-10 years) = Rs 30,000; airbags 50% = Rs 20,000; fibre glass 30% = Rs 7,000; labour Rs 15,000; total Rs 72,000 less salvage Rs 2,000 and deductible Rs 2,000 (car above 1500 cc) = Rs 68,000.

t: A private car (1200 cc) with IDV Rs 2,00,000 has an assessed loss of Rs 1,45,000 after depreciation. The claim payable is
e: Rs 1,45,000 is 72.5% of IDV, below the 75% threshold, so it is a partial loss settled on repair basis: Rs 1,45,000 less compulsory deductible Rs 1,000 = Rs 1,44,000.

t: A taxi (1800 cc, 5 passengers) aged 3 years 9 months is damaged. Assessment before depreciation: metal parts Rs 80,000, plastic parts Rs 20,000, labour Rs 10,000. The insurer's liability is
e: Metal 25% (3-4 years) = Rs 60,000; plastic 50% = Rs 10,000; labour Rs 10,000; total Rs 80,000 less compulsory deductible Rs 1,000 (taxi above 1500 cc) = Rs 79,000.

t: A 20-seater passenger vehicle with IDV Rs 15 lakh has an assessed loss of Rs 1,20,000 after depreciation and no salvage. The amount payable is
e: GR 40: passenger carrying vehicles exceeding 17 but not exceeding 36 passengers carry a compulsory deductible of Rs 1,000 (IMT 21): Rs 1,20,000 - Rs 1,000 = Rs 1,19,000.

t: At renewal a car is 1 year 3 months old and the current ex-showroom price of the model is Rs 15,00,000. The IDV as per schedule is
e: GR 8: 1 to 2 years - 20% depreciation on the current listed price: Rs 15,00,000 x 80% = Rs 12,00,000.

t: The obligatory cession that Indian general insurers must make to GIC Re is currently:
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). The obligatory cession was reduced to 4% from 1 April 2022.

t: An insured enjoying 25% NCB completes another claim-free year. On renewal the OD premium before NCB is Rs 20,000. The NCB amount is
e: The NCB scale is 20%, 25%, 35%, 45%, 50% for 1 to 5 consecutive claim-free years; after 25% the next slab is 35%: 35% of Rs 20,000 = Rs 7,000.

t: A package policy with annual premium Rs 8,000 is issued for 7 months 15 days. The premium chargeable is
e: GR 12: exceeding 7 months but not exceeding 8 months = 90% of annual premium: Rs 7,200. Beyond 8 months the full annual premium is charged.

t: A car with IDV Rs 3,20,000 is laid up and the insured wants theft-only cover without liability under GR 45A. The premium is
e: GR 45A theft only = 0.50% of IDV: Rs 3,20,000 x 0.5% = Rs 1,600 (fire and theft together would be 0.75%).

t: A dealer's Class F package premium is Rs 40,000 and the corresponding liability only premium is Rs 10,000. He wants the radius for used vehicles extended from 160 km to 320 km. The additional premium is
e: Extension for used vehicles up to 320 km costs 25% of the difference between package and liability only premiums: 25% of Rs 30,000 = Rs 7,500 (beyond 320 km it is 50%).

t: A self-drive rental car with IDV Rs 6,00,000 is insured with IMT 35. To cover theft and conversion by the hirer the additional premium under IMT 43 is
e: IMT 43: theft and conversion by the hirer is covered at 1.5% of IDV: Rs 6,00,000 x 1.5% = Rs 9,000; NCB does not apply to this premium.

t: A taxi owner opts at inception to restrict TPPD cover to the statutory Rs 6,000. If the base TP premium is Rs 7,000, the TP premium after the reduction is
e: GR 39 reductions when TPPD is restricted to Rs 6,000: Rs 200 commercial vehicles, Rs 150 taxis, Rs 100 private cars, Rs 50 two wheelers; Rs 7,000 - Rs 150 = Rs 6,850 (IMT 20).

t: A company car is to carry 6 employees (other than the paid driver) and IMT 29 is attached at the tariff rate given in the trainer's notes. The additional premium is
e: The notes give Rs 50 per employee for IMT 28/29, chargeable on the number of employees carried (not exceeding the seating capacity): 6 x Rs 50 = Rs 300. IRDAI has since directed that this cover be given free.
